name: Ashpenaz
overview: Ashpenaz was a male official who served as the chief of Nebuchadnezzar's officials. His role is specifically noted in the book of Daniel, where he is identified by his unique position of authority. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Ashpenaz is a proper name that means 'guest.' This meaning is provided in the biblical reference Daniel 1:3. There are no additional titles or names recorded for him.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Ashpenaz's relationship as the chief official serving under King Nebuchadnezzar. There are no other family relationships or personal connections mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ashpenaz is significant in the biblical narrative as the chief official responsible for overseeing young men taken into Nebuchadnezzar's service. His role highlights the administrative structure of the Babylonian court and sets the stage for the experiences of Daniel and his companions. Through his position, the sovereignty of God is demonstrated as He preserves His servants in a foreign land.
